Header: Echinochloa crus-galli Myanmar: myet-hi; Thailand: hay kai mangda, ya-plong; Vietnam: song chong

Prevention: Only purchase certified crop seed and animal feed to reduce the chance of contamination.
As seeds can travel on animals and machinery, do not allow animals into an affected area, limit machinery use in the area and keep machinery clean to prevent spread.
Keep crop healthy to maximize competitiveness - use optimal water and fertilizer levels.
Some rice cultivars have harmful effects on the weed.
Place mulch over areas where weed is expect to grow – keeps soil cool and surpresses germination.
Most recurring infestations are due to new seed rather than seed in the soil seed bank.
Monitoring: Annual grass, spreading, coarse stalk, tufted, 30-200 cm tall.
Leaves: flat; rough; 65 cm long, 5-30 mm wide.
Stems: grow along ground before turning upward.
Roots: fibrous; multiple root clumps – one clump may spread over an area of 75 cm.
Seeds: one weed plant may produce 40,000; can produce seeds within 60 days.
Seedlings: reddish at base; smooth and green leaves.
Distinguished from other grasses by the absence of ligules (thin outgrowth at leaf-leaf stalk junction) and auricles (ear-shapped appendages at leaf blade-leaf sheath junction).
Young weed is hard to distinguish from young rice crop.
Direct Control: Mowing is unlikely to be effective.
Shallow tillage can reduce weed emergence.
Seeds near to be near the surface to germinate.
Less than 1 cm of soil inhibits germination.
Expose weed to anaerobic fermentation for one month to reduce seed viablility.
Dried lucerne inhibits germination and seedling growth.
Fungi can be used as biological controls e.g.
Exserohilum monoceras , Bipolaris sorokiniana , Curvularia lunata , Bipolaris eleusines and
Check to see if they're available in your country.
For rice, early flooding can surpress the weed.
Flood rice fields ideally with 15-22 cm of water.
Flooding with 2-3 cm water will offer some control.
